quote: I'll email you and and we'll set up a good time, k, when everything's
stewart_read: Customer attempts a classic vague deferral ('I'll email you... set up a good time') with no specific commitment attached — this is the soft-exit pattern the button-up handshake is designed to prevent from happening at all.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be read as genuine intent to follow up later rather than a brush-off, but the vagueness ('when everything's...') without any anchor point supports the soft-exit read.
coaching_implication: Note that the rep did interrupt this deferral rather than accept it — flag this as the correct instinct to reinforce, then show how the later close (02:42-02:53) failed to carry that same discipline through to a locked time.

quote: And what we talked about was showing you our new solar program.
stewart_read: Customer just said he 'wasn't all that impressed' with last year's evaluation — real competitive/historical intel — and the rep moves straight past it into the standard pitch without asking what specifically underwhelmed him.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may be strategically avoiding relitigating a past negative experience to keep momentum toward rebooking, but no evidence shows this was a deliberate choice versus simply not registering the cue.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to ask one follow-up question here — 'what didn't land for you last time?' — since that answer would directly inform what the closer needs to address differently this round.

quote: I can have a special just meet with you if you're available this Saturday.
stewart_read: The rep offers a specific day (Saturday) which is good practice, but the sentence itself is garbled ('I can have a special just meet with you') — an early sign of the scheduling-language looseness that recurs at the close.
alternative_hypothesis: This may be a transcription artifact rather than a rep clarity issue, since Deepgram diarization/transcription errors are noted as a risk in this call.
coaching_implication: Independent of transcription noise, the manager should listen to the audio directly at this timestamp to confirm whether the rep's actual phrasing was clean, since the written line as captured is not confidence-inspiring.

quote: Okay. And you said next Wednesday, that's gonna be the fifteenth at 12:00 worth you?
stewart_read: The rep introduces a '12:00' time that was never discussed anywhere earlier in the call (the only time floated before this was 3PM), muddying the exact appointment slot right as the call is supposed to lock it in.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be a transcription/diarization error rather than the rep actually saying a wrong number, but as recorded it directly contradicts the previously agreed 3PM and is the first sign of the closing confusion.
coaching_implication: Play this exact clip back with the rep — button-up requires one stated time repeated back for confirmation, not three different numbers across ninety seconds.

quote: 3PM. Next Wednesday, I'll do 2PM. Right now. Yep.
stewart_read: In the same breath the rep says '3PM' then immediately says '2PM,' and there is no 'is that fair?' handshake or clean restatement to resolve which time is correct before the call ends.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have simply misspoken and the true time is understood off-transcript by both parties, but nothing in the call recovers or confirms which time is final.
coaching_implication: This is the single most consequential moment in the call: the appointment time is unverifiable from the transcript. Coach the rep to always close with one explicit restated time and an explicit yes/no handshake.

stewart_read: Customer accepts a phone appointment cleanly when offered the choice, which is a genuine cooperative signal rather than a constraint — but the rep never restates the one-hour block or no-driving/computer instructions from button_up after this, skipping the rest of the close protocol.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to follow the channel confirmation immediately with the full button-up sequence (hour block, no driving, computer access) rather than moving straight into text/bill logistics.
